text:
Alex: Heads up — after the 11:02 canary deploy to prod, the canary replica set is crashlooping and the HPA is trying to scale to 0->50 repeatedly. Seeing customer errors on streaming endpoints. Paging oncall.
ops-bot: @oncall triggered paging to #incidents (severity: P1) — incident id INC-20250315-47
Sam: oncall here, looking. Which service?
Alex: service: streaming-ingester-canary (namespace prod-canary). Errors look like OOM and repeated pod restart.
Maria: I see many pods in CrashLoopBackOff and some nodes show MemoryPressure. Also noticed a recent HPA change in the canary manifest: minReplicas: 0 (probable problem).
Sam: ugh, minReplicas 0 for a canary — that lets HPA scale to zero then OOM bursts cause flapping. Can we scale minReplicas to 1 asap?
Liyah: I'll patch it now.
Liyah: running: ```kubectl -n prod-canary patch hpa streaming-ingester-hpa --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":1}]'```
Liyah: patched. HPA now minReplicas=1. Waiting for pods to stabilize.
Chris: logs from one of the crashlooping pods: ```2025-03-15T11:08:12Z ERROR OOMKilled: allocation failed: out of memory
stack: ...
2025-03-15T11:08:13Z INFO restart backoff```
Sam: thanks. Two parallel things: (1) fix HPA minReplicas and resource requests, (2) if this keeps impacting customers we should hit the feature-flag kill-switch or rollback the canary. Maria, can you check feature flag state?
Maria: feature flag for canary routing is `ff.canary.streaming-ingester`. Current state: enabled in prod for 5% of traffic. I can toggle to 0% via console API.
Alex: Product impact: streaming sessions 502/503 for ~5% of requests, onboarding batch ingest delayed. Raised to product-ops.
product-ops: marking incident_severity=P1 due to user-facing errors. Need mitigation ASAP and a customer impact message drafted.
Sam: I'm going to attempt a soft mitigation: reduce canary traffic to 0% (kill-switch) and hold rollout. Maria, flip it.
Maria: doing API call: ```curl -X POST "https://flags.prod.internal/api/v1/toggle" -d '{"flag":"ff.canary.streaming-ingester","percentage":0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****'```
Maria: response: `\{\"status\":\"ok\"\}` — canary traffic now 0%. Observability should stop receiving canary requests.
Sam: Monitoring — error rate dropped for streaming endpoints but some canary pods still crashlooping on nodes. We need to decide: patch resources and let canary recover, or rollback helm release. Thoughts?
Chris: Some nodes were cordoned during the deploy by the deploy job: `kubectl drain` on node-7 failed and left pods in evicted state, causing pressure on other nodes. That contributed to OOMs. I think rollback is safest while we audit manifests.
Sam: Agreed. Maria, can you queue a helm rollback for canary release to previous revision? Keep the canary label but rollback container image and env changes.
Maria: running: ```deploy-bot: helm rollback streaming-ingester-canary 3 --namespace prod-canary```
deploy-bot: rollback started, release streaming-ingester-canary -> revision 3 (in progress)
Liyah: I'm also scaling affected deployment down to 0 to stop crashloops while rollback completes: ```kubectl -n prod-canary scale deploy streaming-ingester-canary --replicas=0```
Sam: good. Once rollback finishes we'll scale up to 1 with corrected resources.
deploy-bot: rollback complete. Release streaming-ingester-canary now at revision 3.
Liyah: scaling back up: ```kubectl -n prod-canary scale deploy streaming-ingester-canary --replicas=1```
Liyah: scaled. Waiting on pod to become Ready.
Sam: Pod launched, initial health checks passing. No new OOMs in logs so far.
Chris: I uncordoned node-7 after verifying the drain state and cleared evicted pods backlog: ```kubectl uncordon node-7``` — nodes look stable now.
Alex: customer-facing: error rate for streaming endpoints down to baseline. Product-ops, please publish customer note.
product-ops: drafting message: "We experienced errors for a subset of streaming requests due to a canary rollout misconfiguration. We have rolled back the canary and disabled canary traffic. No ongoing impact; monitoring continues." Will send after Sam thumbs up.
Sam: 👍 sounds accurate. Add note that internal root cause looks like HPA minReplicas set to 0 + a problematic drain during deploy leading to OOMs.
product-ops: added that line. Sending now.
Alex: quick postmortem TODOs: - prevent minReplicas=0 on canaries via admission webhook or CI lint - block drain during canary window or require manual approval - add automated kill-switch runbook and button in console - add pre-deploy HPA sanity checks to CI
Maria: I created a short runbook in docs repo and filed a ticket: DOCS-1194 to add runbook. Also filed an incident ticket INC-20250315-47 (link internal).
Sam: handing off to eng-sre for follow-up. I'll remain reachable for questions.
ops-bot: incident INC-20250315-47 status -> mitigated. Please attach logs and mark for postmortem.
Chris: attaching quick logs and `kubectl get hpa` output in the incident doc.
Liyah: closing loop — canary deploy will be blocked until we push fixes. I'll add CI gating.
Alex: thanks everyone. We'll run a brief postmortem tomorrow and include action owners.
Sam: closing thread here, follow-ups tracked in the ticket.
product-ops: incident status set to resolved for customers, will keep internal open until postmortem complete.
